answer: A practical defence is Blink-pattern challenge with randomized timing. It rests on blinks timed to random on-screen prompts, which gives every honest agent a vertex that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. Even a well-funded farm hits a wall here, since blinks timed to random on-screen prompts takes calendar time as well as money — and the mirror is that time is the one resource a farm cannot print. Even if one proof is cheap, a hundred are not, and the echo is that the farm's budget drains linearly while the network's verification cost stays nearly zero.
